commands.summary: Describes the running Caliper app: its version, the ABI epoch its applets must be built for, the services it offers, and the versions of the SDK, libtorch and its interface libraries. It changes nothing.

reason.description: Why the applet cannot run; empty for a READY applet.

status.description: READY, ACTIVE, REFUSED or SHADOWED, as caliper list prints it.

commands.summary: Lists the applets the app found, as caliper list shows them: each applet's manifest id, its version, its kind (library or spec), its folder, its status (READY, ACTIVE for the one open now, REFUSED, SHADOWED) and the reason when it cannot run. The id is what app.launch takes. It changes nothing.

id.description: The applet's manifest id, such as com.example.my-viewer, from app.applets.

commands.name: app.launch

already_open.description: Whether the applet's page was already open.

note.description: With PENDING_APPROVAL or PENDING: what the launch waits for, and that spec.get names the open spec once it has opened.

status.description: The applet's status after the launch: ACTIVE when it opened; PENDING_APPROVAL when its open waits for the person's approval, because it would replace the open spec's unsaved changes; PENDING when the app cannot tell yet whether it will.

commands.summary: Opens the page of one applet, as a click on its row on the app's landing screen does. The page shown before is closed first; an attached live session stays attached. The id is an applet's manifest id from app.applets. A dashboard of the workspace opens with an applet.open from your origin, so when it would replace the open spec's unsaved changes it waits for the person's approval: the status is then PENDING_APPROVAL rather than ACTIVE, and its note says how to check whether it opened.

commands.summary: Creates a loader for each file path given, choosing the reader from the file's extension (csv, tsv, parquet, json, jsonl, arrow, npy, npz, safetensors, hdf5, png, jpg, wav), and runs the new loaders unless run is false, so that the files' contents appear in the catalog as table: and tensor: sources. Paths are relative to the workspace; a path outside it is accepted only from the person's own drop or file dialog. Pickle files are refused. Undo deletes the loaders it created and their outputs.

commands.summary: Saves a new loader from its TOML recipe, as loaders/<id>.loader.toml in the workspace, and runs it when run is true. The recipe holds caliper_loader = 0; a [loader] table with id and title; an [input] table with path (a file or glob relative to the workspace) and an optional reader; optional [reader] options; and one or more [[output]] tables, each with a name and an optional SQL SELECT over the relation input, or a tensor to select. It fails when a loader with that id exists. Undo deletes it.

run.description: Whether to run the loader at once; false when absent.

text.description: The new recipe as TOML text.

examples.text:
caliper_loader = 0
[loader]
id = "run42-metrics"
title = "Run 42"
[input]
path = "data/run42/*.parquet"
[[output]]
name = "run42_metrics"
sql = "SELECT step, loss FROM input WHERE step > 0"

The id comes from loader.list.

commands.name: spec.new
commands.summary: Starts a new, empty spec and makes it the open spec: the one the builder shows and that the source, panel and layout commands edit. A spec is the text that describes an applet built from data: its sources, its panels and their layout. The id names the applet, in lower case with digits, - and _. Undo returns to the spec that was open before.

path.description: The spec file, relative to the workspace.

commands.name: spec.open

id.description: The applet id of the spec opened.

path.description: The file opened, relative to the workspace.

warnings.description: What the validator warns about, such as a source with no wire form.

code.description: A stable code, such as spec.unknown_primitive or spec.not_portable.

message.description: One plain sentence that says what is wrong.

where.description: Where in the spec: a path such as panel[2].bind.y, or a line and column such as 12:7; empty when it is not located.

commands.summary: Opens a spec file of the workspace as the open spec. The path is relative to the workspace and ends in .spec.toml, such as applets/attention-entropy/attention-entropy.spec.toml. To open a saved applet by its id, use applet.open. Undo returns to the spec that was open before, with its unsaved changes.

applet.description: A saved spec applet's id, from applet.list; the open spec when absent.

commands.name: spec.get

dirty.description: Whether it has changes that are not saved.

json.description: The spec's canonical JSON form: the TOML tables as JSON objects, as the spec format's JSON Schema describes them.

open.description: True with a spec in the result, the open one or the named applet's; false when no applet is named and no spec is open, and then no other field is given.

path.description: Its file, relative to the workspace, or null when it was never saved.

text.description: The spec as TOML text, in canonical form.

commands.summary: Returns the open spec as its TOML text and as its canonical JSON form, with its applet id, the file it was saved to or opened from, and whether it has unsaved changes. With applet, it returns that saved spec applet's spec instead, read from its files without opening it. When no spec is open and no applet is named, it answers open false and nothing else, which is not an error: make one with spec.new or open one with spec.open or applet.open. It changes nothing.

dry_run.description: Whether to check the change and return its diff without applying it, so that it can be shown for approval first; false when absent.

text.description: The whole spec as TOML text, with caliper_spec = 0, an [applet] table, [[source]] and [[panel]] tables and a [layout] table.

examples.text:
caliper_spec = 0
[applet]
id = "loss"
title = "Loss"
[[source]]
id = "loss"
sql = "SELECT step, loss FROM run42_metrics ORDER BY step"
[[panel]]
id = "loss"
primitive = "series"
bind = { x = "loss.step", y = ["loss.loss"] }
[layout]
children = ["loss"]

commands.summary: Replaces the whole layout of the open spec. The layout is a flat list of nodes: each node splits its space horizontally or vertically between its children, with ratio the share of the first child, or shows them in tabs. A child is a panel id or another node's id, and root names the top node, or the one panel when there is only one. Every panel of the spec should appear once; a panel left out is not drawn. Undo restores the previous layout. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied.

commands.summary: Starts a preview of the open spec: a scratch copy on which edits of the open spec stack, each checked like a real edit, while the open spec, the undo history and the journal stay as they are. An edit reaches the preview when its call names the preview's id, which Caliper API takes in the X-Caliper-Preview header; spec.get, spec.validate and panel.render read the preview the same way. With panel or source the preview is scoped to that target: its edits may change only the target, the sources a target panel binds and the items the preview adds. preview.diff shows the stacked change, and only the person commits it, with Accept in Caliper. A preview ends when it is committed or discarded, or after 30 minutes without use.

Only the person commits a preview, with Accept in Caliper: a call from an agent, from caliper-mcp or from a program is refused with preview.not_allowed. When the open spec changed since the edits were made, they are applied to it again, and when one no longer applies the commit is refused with history.conflict and nothing changes.
